answer: The defense I trust is resource-weighted membership: an identity must lock a stake costly to acquire, and payouts follow locked value, not account count. A farmer spawning ten thousand identities earns what one honest holder with the same capital earns, so each extra one is a weak signal the network can discount. Collusion slashes that stake, so the attacker risks real value and burning it cannot bend the reward curve. Membership becomes a bond, a willow planted at your own cost, not umber paint hiding rot. Attack cost scales with account count while payout stays flat, so profit vanishes.
